purpose: Financial primary-document retrieval and extracted-text anchor audit
limitations: This is a curated 12-case known-document benchmark, not open-web recall or a service-level estimate.
Planned queries and read windows are declared in the fixture. This does not measure autonomous model query planning, page selection, or final financial judgment accuracy.

Baseline uses one natural query; planned uses that same query plus a semantic source-aware query. Both use the same date boundary. Each Serper request asks for ten results; the merged output retains up to twenty.
Gold URLs and titles are used only to identify retrieved documents. They are not inserted into search queries or fetched as retrieval fallbacks.

Anchor coverage means declared value, period, and unit literals occur in the returned read window. It does not establish their relationship, table-column alignment, or factual correctness of a final answer.
Search and page dates are metadata claims, not archived proof of historical public availability. Unknown dates remain explicitly unverified.
This benchmark does not evaluate news freshness, relevance precision across all candidates, paywalled sources, OCR, or model reasoning.
